title: Apple's window to appeal the EU General Court's DMA gatekeeper-designation ruling to the CJEU closes
source: NEWS: the deadline's PROCEDURAL RULE is now read directly off the Court of Justice's own press release, upgrading the proposal's press-relayed version. curia.europa.eu Press Release No 96/26 (Luxembourg, 8 July 2026, 'Judgment of the General Court in Joined Cases T-1079/23, T-1080/23 | Apple v Commission and T-214/24 Apple and Apple Distribution International v Commission'), PDF fetched direct this session (curia.europa.eu/site/upload/docs/application/pdf/2026-07/cp260096en.pdf, HTTP 200, 120,204 bytes) and its text layer decompressed locally (node/zlib, the same technique the missouri-map-tro-expiry-2026-09-22 ledger used), states verbatim in its closing NOTE: 'An appeal, limited to points of law only, may be brought before the Court of Justice against the decision of the General Court within two months and ten days of notification of the decision.' The press release also confirms the ruling itself: the General Court 'dismisses all the actions brought by Apple. It confirms the designation of Apple as a gatekeeper in relation to the App Store and iOS, and finds the actions concerning the iMessage service to be inadmissible.' The exact deadline DATE remains a computation, not a primary statement: the rule runs from 'notification of the decision', which is not necessarily 8 July (the delivery date) — the Court's own press release does not state the notification date, so 'around September 18' (MacObserver, 2026-09-13, applying delivery-date + 2mo10d as a proxy) stays the best available estimate, corroborated independently by Euronews, Courthouse News, JURIST, Concurrences, digitalpolicyalert.org and FSFE (all fetched or searched direct 2026-09-17), none of which states a notification date either. Status stays estimate on two independent grounds: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts (IR:/CAL:/BLS:/FED:/PJM:/SEC:/TSY:/OCC:/BEA:/CENSUS:/ISM:/CB:/UMICH:/FHFA:) has no slot for a CJEU procedural deadline, and the notification-date gap above means even a primary Court source would not remove the date's own estimate character. A targeted search this session (2026-09-17, one day before the window) found no report of Apple having filed an appeal, declined to appeal, or announced a decision; Apple's own 8 July statement ('We will continue advocating for the innovation and privacy our European customers deserve') does not confirm appeal intent either way.
notes: Canonical file written from the single proposal, proposals/apple-dma-gatekeeper-cjeu-appeal-deadline-2026-09-18.from-apple-eu-dma-terms-2026-10-01.json (filed 2026-09-17 during that entry's own pulse-check adjacency sweep). This is a DIFFERENT, THIRD Apple-EU-DMA matter from the two the apple-eu-dma-terms-2026-10-01 ledger already tracks as 'overhang not retired' — the still-pending €500M anti-steering fine appeal (T-438/25) and the live DMA.100203/100204 interoperability specification proceedings. This entry is the appeal window on the gatekeeper-designation challenge the General Court dismissed 2026-07-08 (Joined Cases T-1079/23, T-1080/23, T-214/24) — a fourth data point on the same overhang, not a duplicate of the other three. Low impact: a procedural filing deadline, not a scheduled disclosure or ruling. If Apple appeals, the CJEU appeal itself would run for months to years with no near-term market read (points-of-law-only review); if the window lapses, that forecloses this one line of challenge to the gatekeeper designation while DMA compliance itself is already priced in (Apple settled and implemented its EU business-terms changes on 2026-08-18, effective 2026-10-01 — see apple-eu-dma-terms-2026-10-01) and the €500M fine appeal and interoperability proceedings continue untouched either way.
